label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Mr. Bergeron, Hélène here. You are right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid for bread in advance. My nephew showed me this thread, and I can see that our little sign has caused a lot more worry than excitement. I am sorry about that.

So here is the news I was trying to keep for the reopening: **Le Pétrin Doré is not closing or moving. I bought the building!**

Marc-Antoine, your cousin is half right. The building was sold, but it was sold to the baker downstairs. We signed at the notary on December 15. There will be no bank, no vape shop, and no condos replacing the apartments. There will be bread, as there has been at our corner of Fairmount since March 2009. And, finally, there will be somewhere to sit down and eat it.

But first, because this is what you asked about, let me answer very clearly about the carnets.

**Every carnet is still valid. There is no expiry date.** We sold 214 in October, at $60 for 12 loaves, and we will honour every loaf still owed. If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves left. The two weeks of work in January do not change that, and neither does the change in ownership of the building.

If anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me at the bakery. I will refund the unused part of your carnet, no questions asked. You do not have to argue your case or explain yourself. It is your money.

Also, every carnet holder can have a free croissant in January. A small thank-you, and an apology for the worry caused by that sign.

I will be honest: reading the word “scam” hurt. I have been making bread on this street for nearly 17 years. That is a long time, and the trust people put in me matters very much. But I also understand that you cannot know what is happening behind a closed door if all I give you is “big news soon.” People have seen enough small shops disappear from Mile End. I should have been clearer, and I would rather explain things properly now than have a fight with my neighbours.

Here is exactly what is happening in January.

**We will be closed from January 4 through January 18 for work, and we will reopen on Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

We are getting a new four-deck oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven is from 1998, and it has broken down three times this year. I have some affection for it, but I am ready for an oven that gives us fewer unpleasant surprises.

We are also taking over the space at the back that used to be the dépanneur’s storage room. That will give us room for six small tables. Not a big café, just a few places where you can sit with your coffee and your bread instead of having to take everything away. I have wanted to offer that for a long time.

And to answer the concern about the people living upstairs: **the three apartments will stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I have made that promise to them in writing. This is their home. Buying the building does not mean asking them to leave it.

I also want to say a little about M. Ferland, because he is part of this story. He is 81 now and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. Before offering the building to anybody else, he offered to sell it to me.

He has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette, “pas trop cuite.” At the notary he cried a little. So when I say this is good news, it is not only because we are getting a new oven. Being able to buy the place where I have worked all these years means a great deal to me. I wanted to tell everyone when the work was finished and we could celebrate together. Clearly, keeping it a surprise was not my best idea.

The sign was written by my nephew Thomas at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking about how it might look to someone walking past. Please do not blame him. I approved it. We meant it as happy news, not a mysterious warning.

As for the half-empty shelves on the 28th, that was the aftermath of Christmas, not us clearing out the business. We sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches. Nothing about those shelves meant that we were leaving.

Priya, thank you for your kind words. And thank you to everyone who defended us, who worried about losing us, or who simply wanted to know where their next pain de campagne was coming from. Even in an upsetting thread, it is good to find out that the bakery would be missed.

Now that the surprise is out, please come celebrate with us on **Saturday, January 23**. We will already be back at work from Tuesday the 19th, but Saturday is our reopening celebration. Everyone is invited for a free coffee and a piece of the new bread. Carnet holders, regulars, neighbours who have never come inside, and people from this thread too.

Mr. Bergeron, thank you for asking me directly. The answer is that we are staying, your carnets are good, and I hope this is news we can all be happy about.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
